what_changed: End of training: no change since 5,800; final OBS values accuracy 1.000, OOD_DEV 0.647, block IIA 0.941, pooled persistent edit 0.975, interaction 0.395; A and B identical at all 61 checkpoints (no edit installed).
hypothesis: Summary of this network's development, for the sealed comparison: a zero-plus-constant plateau (100-1,000); discrete-log circle at 1,100; fast formation 1,100-1,500 with two balanced mass writers (heads 0 and 3) whose unit splits partly cancel, giving a canonical-like, highly editable block; post-convergence oscillation of held-out accuracy carried by near-margin inputs; a held-out failure located upstream in mass formation for unseen unit-value pairs, with structured default-unit fallbacks for acceleration and unstructured errors for mass.
evidence: Journal steps 100-5,900: Level-2 tools (predictions, ood_locus, heads, patch, sharpness), two OBS dry runs (1,500, 1,800) showing registered organisational edits cost held-out accuracy, read-only snapshot and copy analyses (bias swap, margins, error structure, writer scaling); causal claims rest on interchange, ablation and copy tests, probes reported as descriptive only.
key_question: Does the sealed evaluation (FINAL, OOD_FINAL) confirm the OBS / OOD_DEV picture, including the add-one held-out edit (never measured during training)?
intervention_rationale: Across 60 reviews no registered intervention had a credible predicted benefit without a generalisation cost: the network was highly editable from formation on, and the diagnosed defect (upstream held-out mass formation) lies outside the registered primitives. Two new primitives (layer-1 compositional binding supervision; checkpoint-anchored upstream regularisation) are proposed for a future registration.
previous_interventions: none installed; two dry runs (1,500 interaction removal: OOD_DEV -0.017; 1,800 upstream OOD-targeted: -0.026); early-phase candidates never submitted
